name: dropdown
description: A button and a panel of links and buttons that opens under it, closing on Escape or a click outside, with no script unless it is asked to open on hover.

attributes.name: data-side
attributes.description: Which edge of the trigger the panel lines up with.

attributes.name: data-trigger
attributes.description: What opens the panel. Click always works; hover adds opening under the pointer, and needs the optional module and a pointer that hovers.

children.description: The trigger; its popovertarget names the panel's id.
The panel, holding ordinary links and buttons.

tokens.name: --yeti-dropdown-open-delay
tokens.description: How long the pointer must rest before a hover-triggered panel opens.

tokens.name: --yeti-dropdown-close-delay
tokens.description: How long a hover-triggered panel waits after the pointer leaves before closing.

keyboard.action: On the trigger, opens or closes the panel.
Walks the items, which are ordinary links and buttons.
Closes the panel and returns focus to the trigger.

a11y.notes: With data-trigger="hover" the module adds opening under the pointer and changes nothing else: the click, the keyboard, focus and the expanded state are all still the browser's, and a pointer that cannot hover never gets it. The trigger needs a name, and the browser sets its expanded state from popovertarget. The items are deliberately ordinary links and buttons with no menu roles: role="menu" promises arrow-key semantics that belong to application menus, and on a website a disclosure panel is both simpler and better announced. Inside a nav, put the dropdown in the li beside the link it belongs to.

guarded: anchor positioning (fallback: the panel is centred by the user agent)
